newsitem.title: LEBANON: Hizbollah rockets Israeli posts in south Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Hizbollah rockets Israeli posts in south Lebanon.

text.p: Hizbollah guerrillas fired two salvoes of Katyusha rockets at Israeli and allied militia posts in south Lebanon on Tuesday, wounding two Lebanese civilians, pro-Israeli militia sources said.
Two rockets landed on a farm near the South Lebanon Army (SLA) militia outpost of Dimeshkieeh, injuring a farmer and his 15-year-old son, the militia sources said.
Earlier, Hizbollah said it fired Katyushas towards Israeli and SLA militia outposts in retaliation for Israeli shelling on Monday night that killed two Lebanese civilians in south Lebanon.
Israeli security sources in Jerusalem said a mortar or Katyusha rocket slammed into northern Israel.
"The Katyusha rocketing was in response for the continued violation of April 1996 understanding which bans firing on civilians," a Hizbollah spokesman told Reuters after the early morning rocketing.
The April 1996 ceasefire understanding which ended a 17-day Israeli onslaught on Lebanon which killed about 200 people -- mainly civilians -- bars Israel and Hizbollah from hitting civilian targets.

Israeli shelling on Monday night killed two civilians in the village of Berti, east of the southern port city of Sidon. The shelling took place after two SLA militiamen were wounded in a Hizbollah rocket attack on their outpost.
Israeli warplanes also raided suspected Hizbollah positions in the south.
The 3,000-strong SLA militia helps some 1,000 Israeli troops hold a 15-km (nine miles)-deep occupation zone in south Lebanon.
Hizbollah (Party of God) almost daily attacks Israeli and SLA posts and patrols in a bid to drive the Israelis from the occupation zone.
